title: Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the University of Tennessee and UCOR for Areas of Potential Collaboration & Cooperation
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: Mr. Mullis will discuss the memorandum of understanding outlineing the collaboration between the University of Tennessee and UCOR, focusing on joint efforts in nuclear forensics, technical services, decommissioning, environmental restoration, and nuclear safety. The agreement aims to develop research programs, enhance training and educational opportunities for UCOR employees and UT students, facilitate internships and mentorships, and support post-graduate career pathways and senior design projects, ultimately strengthening both organizations’ technical capabilities and workforce development.

topic: CCPS Process Safety Student Boot Camp: Advancing Process Safety Education through Industry Collaboration
title: CCPS Process Safety Student Boot Camp: Advancing Process Safety Education through Industry Collaboration
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: As part of a global initiative to accelerate Process Safety education and integrate real-world industry experience into academic learning, CCPS launched the Student Boot Camp program in 2015. Since its inception, CCPS has partnered with several CCPS member companies to deliver this impactful program to students at over 45 universities across the United States and one university in China. This intensive two-day course is led by two seasoned CCPS instructors—each bringing over 25 years of hands-on experience in Process Safety from sectors including chemicals, petrochemicals, oil & gas, and broader manufacturing industries. The core learning objectives of the Student Boot Camp include: Introducing students to how leading global companies effectively manage Process Safety to prevent catastrophic incidents involving toxic, flammable, and highly reactive materials. Providing students an opportunity to engage directly with experienced professionals—sharing lessons learned, exploring real-world scenarios, and discussing their own internship or co-op experiences. Facilitating interactive breakout sessions where students apply Risk-Based Process Safety (RBPS) elements and key Process Safety concepts in practical group exercises. Reinforcing learning through in-depth case studies of actual incidents to highlight key principles and the importance of robust safety systems. The course begins by establishing foundational Process Safety concepts, including the Anatomy of an Incident, Loss of Containment, Containment and Control, and Layers of Protection Analysis—both preventive and mitigative. The curriculum then explores each of the 20 RBPS elements, emphasizing their individual and collective roles in achieving Process Safety excellence. Each element is paired with a relevant incident case study to underscore its real-world implications and the critical importance of effective implementation. A capstone team exercise on Day 2 integrates all course learnings, allowing students to apply their knowledge in a simulated, systems-based scenario. The CCPS Student Boot Camp continues to serve as a powerful bridge between academia and industry, equipping the next generation of engineers with the mindset, tools, and understanding necessary to lead with safety and most importantly, raising the safety culture thinking early in their operating journey.

topic: Unlocking Innovation: The Power of Academic Partnerships in Manufacturing
title: Unlocking Innovation: The Power of Academic Partnerships in Manufacturing
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: MxD (Manufacturing x Digital) is the nation’s digital manufacturing institute, a public-private partnership that brings together industry, academia, and government to drive innovation and strengthen U.S. manufacturing. By convening a diverse ecosystem of collaborators, MxD delivers real-world solutions to some of the sector’s most pressing challenges—from workforce development to cybersecurity and digital transformation. This session will highlight MxD’s role as a convener and catalyst, sharing best practices and lessons learned in leading effective cross-sector partnerships that accelerate the deployment of cutting-edge manufacturing technologies.

topic: Placing Your Bets on Your Innovation Portfolio: The Kelly Method for Innovation Portfolio Budgeting.
title: Placing Your Bets on Your Innovation Portfolio: The Kelly Method for Innovation Portfolio Budgeting.
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: How to place your bets on projects in your innovation portfolio? Innovation or capital budget portfolios can have 100s of projects. Stage Gate methods are commonly used, often supplemented by NPV or ROI estimates. However, the role of risk and probability is not always properly included, and many decisions are made one project at a time. In this talk we test the Kelly Method for allocating resources among the projects, going beyond simple go-kill-pause decisions to more precise decisions about what fraction of the budget to allocate to each project. Risk is explicitly factored into an algorithm, and the entire portfolio is numerically optimized simultaneously. The method is tested on a real portfolio, and results are presented for the allocation and improvement in IRR. In addition, the concept of “buckets” are included as optimization constraints to allow customization of the method. We’ll discuss how the Kelly Method can improve profitability, improve internal technical-commercial communication and focus, and give you greater peace of mind as you make critical innovation resourcing decisions for your company.
